title: Step Composition Association Coordination Contract

scope.purpose: Define reusable association-coordination invariants for Step-internal runtime components whose specialized contracts define association with Step-owned target scopes.
scope.applicability: Applies only when a concrete Step selects a component pattern that defines an association. It does not require every component, SPU, or Step to participate in an association.

architecturalPosition.nature: A cross-cutting coordination contract governing association relationships and their use by Step Composition.
notAComponentType: Does not define a Generic Supporting Unit or a universal runtime component type.
Does not define a base class, interface, callable signature, association object layout, registry, manager, or runtime service.
Does not replace the specialized Behavioral, Association, or Lifecycle Contract of any component pattern.
architecturalPosition.authority: The concrete Step owns its Step Composition. Step Composition remains authoritative for association decisions within that Step.
architecturalPosition.specialization: Each component pattern retains its own identity names, association mechanics, target-access semantics, compatibility rules, and any additional constraints.

coreConcepts.association: An explicit relationship between one concrete Step-internal runtime component instance and one target scope within the owning Step instance.
coreConcepts.associationTarget: The Step-owned scope to which the component is applicable under the association. It is not necessarily the exact subject/resource acted upon by every invocation or operation.
coreConcepts.associationIdentity: The identity of the relationship itself, distinct from the component instance and target identities.
coreConcepts.invocationBinding: The explicit selection of one association context under which a particular invocation or activity is authorized.

conceptualIdentityRoles.meaning: Identifies the concrete runtime instance participating in the association.
Identifies the target scope, including its scope kind and concrete target instance.
Identifies one particular relationship between that component instance and that target scope within the owning Step.
Identifies one invocation/activity and remains distinct from instance, association, and target identities.

rules: The conceptual identity roles are mandatory distinctions; their literal field names and representations are defined by each specialized contract.
A component instance identity must not be derived from or overloaded to represent an association or target identity.
An association identity identifies exactly one component-instance-to-target relationship within one owning Step instance.
Each distinct relationship has a distinct association identity, even when the component instance or target is shared.
Identities remain unique and interpretable for as long as active work or retained evidence may refer to them; no UUID, counter, address, timestamp, or other generation mechanism is mandated.
Ending and later recreating a relationship requires a new association identity whenever prior relationship evidence may remain observable.
The target identity must distinguish target scope kind as well as concrete target instance; a component identity alone is insufficient to identify a different scope kind.

permittedConceptualKinds: A specific SPU instance or SPU-defined internal scope.
The owning Step instance as a whole.
Another explicitly identified Step-internal scope, component, processing boundary, or context defined by the concrete Step.
invariants: The target belongs to the owning Step's internal composition.
The target is identified independently of the associated component instance and association.
Association does not transfer ownership of the target or its resources to the associated component.
The target scope expresses applicability/authorization context; the exact data or resource acted upon is defined by the specialized invocation or operation contract.
specialization: The concrete Step defines permitted target kinds, target identity representation, compatibility, access mode, and target lifetime.
The concrete Step defines whether target access is a snapshot, immutable view, borrowed reference, live query, callback, handle, subscription surface, or another mechanism.
Target access validity and resource lifetime are not inferred from association identity alone.

multiplicityAndCompatibility.frameworkRule: No universal cardinality, exclusivity, or sharing rule is imposed.
allowedWhenSpecialized: One component instance may participate in multiple associations.
Multiple component instances may be associated with the same target.
A target may have no associated component.
specializationMustDefine: Whether an instance may have multiple simultaneous associations.
Whether a target may have multiple associated instances.
Any cardinality, exclusivity, sharing, compatibility, or ordering constraints.
Whether associations may change during active invocations or protected processing intervals.

stepComposition: Selects which component instances participate in the Step's internal composition.
Establishes, validates, activates where applicable, changes, rebinds, deactivates, and ends associations.
Maintains authoritative association-to-instance-and-target correspondence for the period required by active work and retained evidence.
Selects the applicable association for each invocation or activity.
Coordinates association changes and dissociation without silently redirecting in-flight work or invalidating retained evidence.
associatedComponent: Consumes the association context supplied or authorized for its invocation/activity.
Operates only within the supplied target scope and access capabilities.
May report unusability or request an association change through Step Composition.
Does not independently create, select, mutate, rebind, or terminate its associations.
targetComponent: May expose or withdraw target-specific access capabilities under its own contract.
Does not acquire ownership of the associated component or authority over its association merely by being the target.
outerLevels: Stage Composition invokes the owning Step and does not manage its internal associations.
Pipeline does not impose a global association registry, topology, or manager.

generalPreconditions: The owning Step instance and associated component instance are identifiable within the Step's composition.
The target scope is identifiable and belongs to the owning Step's internal composition.
The component satisfies the lifecycle eligibility conditions required by its specialized contract for association.
The component capability is compatible with the target under the concrete Step's specialization.
The association identity is valid and unique within its required observation scope.
associationValidity.authority: Step Composition validates and enforces association validity. Specialized contracts may add semantic checks and more restrictive preconditions.
separation: Association existence is not equivalent to technical readiness.
Association existence is not equivalent to lifecycle admission unless the specialized lifecycle contract explicitly defines that dependency.
Association existence is not invocation authorization.
Association does not itself activate observation, processing, or handling behavior.

invocationBinding.rule: Whenever a specialized component invocation or activity is authorized under an association, it is bound to exactly one selected association and the target identity bound to that association.
invariants: Step Composition explicitly selects the association for each invocation when an instance has multiple associations.
The supplied association target identity must match the selected association.
The component must not infer, substitute, or silently broaden the association scope.
An invocation already authorized under an association remains attributable to that original association even if the association changes or ends while work is in progress.
Repeated invocations receive distinct invocation identities, even when the same component instance and association are reused.

An invocation's exact subject, validation target, observation subject, error occurrence, or operation resource is defined by the specialized behavior contract and need not equal the association target.

changeRules: Association mutability is not mandated; the concrete Step defines whether changes are permitted.

A change that alters the component participant or target is represented as ending the prior relationship and establishing a new association identity unless the specialization defines a safe in-place change with preserved identity semantics.
A change must not silently redirect an already-authorized invocation or rewrite provenance already retained.
dissociationRules: Step Composition decides and records the effective end of an association.
From the effective end point, the association cannot authorize new invocations or activities.
The concrete Step defines whether in-flight work completes under the original association, is cancelled, or is reconciled before dissociation is considered complete.
Dissociation does not by itself destroy, release, or replace the component instance.
Dissociation does not invalidate accepted outputs or historical evidence produced under the association.
Ending one association does not implicitly end other associations of the same instance.
historicalEvidence: Retained evidence preserves sufficient association, target, component, Step, and invocation provenance for its interpretation.
Historical identity metadata may outlive the runtime component and target objects.
Retaining identity metadata does not require retaining the runtime instance, target handles, borrowed views, callbacks, or resource leases.

required: Map each conceptual identity role to the specialized identity names, representations, issuers, and uniqueness scopes.
Define target kinds, target identity semantics, and Step-membership validation.
Define component-target compatibility and any multiplicity/exclusivity constraints.
Define association establishment, activation, change, and dissociation conditions.
Define how each invocation/activity receives its exact association context and target access.
Define in-flight behavior during association change or dissociation.
Define the minimum historical provenance retained by each specialized output or evidence type.
specializationRequirements.completionRule: A specialization is association-coordination complete when identity roles, target scope, compatibility, multiplicity, authority, invocation binding, change/dissociation, in-flight work, and historical provenance are explicit.

explicitNonGoals: No Generic Supporting Unit abstraction or universal component base type.
No mandatory association for every Step-internal component.
No universal target kind, cardinality, exclusivity, or sharing policy.
No transfer of ownership or lifecycle authority to the target.
No automatic invocation, activation, readiness, release, or result aggregation caused by association establishment.
No universal association registry, service, graph, or runtime manager.
No universal invocation signature or result schema.

references.relationship: Defines Step Composition ownership and authority over Step-internal composition and flow.
